interface.name: skyq_shell
interface.description:
The skyq_shell interface is exposed as a global object enabling clients to turn their wl_surfaces into skyq_surfaces for controlling how they are displayed.
In addition the skyq_shell interface generates events to signal state change of the client, for example if it has lost input focus or has been requested to go into suspend mode.

enum.name: skyq_surface_flags

description.summary: flags to set when getting the skyq surface

enum.description: These flags are used to inform how the skyq_surface is expected to be used.

entry.name: overlay

description.summary: create the surface as an overlay

entry.description:
Overlay surfaces are displayed at the top of the z-order above all running applications. By default when displayed they automatically grab the input focus and the focus is only returned to the running app once the surface is hidden or destroyed. This can be changed by setting the transparent_to_input flag.
Setting this flag can only be set / cleared while the surface is not visible.
Creating an overlay surface is a privileged operation and the window manager may decide to block the request if the calling app lacks the correct permissions.

entry.name: transparent_for_input

description.summary: makes the surface transparent for input

entry.description:
Setting this flag means the surface will never receive input events.
This flag can only be combined with the overlay flag, and is typically used to display short transient popup surfaces.
The flag can be set when the surface is visible or hidden.

request.name: set_surface_flags

description.summary: hides a surface raised as a notification

request.description: Sets the flags on a simple-shell surface. This is used to mark surfaces as Popup or Notification types, which the window manager will handle differently when made visible. It is not possible to change the surface flags once a buffer has been drawn.

arg.name: surfaceId
arg.summary: surface id value returned by the wl-simple-shell interface

entry.name: forbidden
entry.summary: tried to set notification or popup flag without capability

enum.name: state
enum.description: All apps are in one of these states...

entry.name: active
entry.summary: the app is active one on screen

entry.name: inactive
entry.summary: the app is visible but input focus is currently with another app (ie. notification overlay shown)

entry.name: hidden
entry.summary: the app is not visible and not active

entry.name: suspended
entry.summary: the app has been suspended and should save settings and tear down gfx etc

entry.name: hibernated
entry.summary: the app is hibernated or entering hibernating state

event.name: state_changed

description.summary: the state of the app has changed

event.description: This is a notification that the state of the app has changed from the POV of the window manager. It is up to the app to act on the state change ...

event.name: close

description.summary: request for the app to shut down

event.description: In response to this event the application is expected to clean up and shutdown. Once this event is sent the app will no longer by able to display anything on screen and won't receive any key presses.

entry.name: visible_by_default
entry.summary: surfaces are automatically visible when created

request.name: set_visibility_policy

description.summary: sets the default visibility policy for surfaces

request.description: Westeros sets all surfaces to visible when they are created, this clashes with some windowing code (Qt) which expects surfaces to initially be invisible. This in turn can cause some artifacts when the surface / window is first created. This API allows you to change the default policy so the westeros behavior is matched to the windowing code. The policy can be changed dynamically and applies to any surfaces created after the call.

request.name: set_suspended

description.summary: signals the window manager that the app has suspended itself

request.description: This should be called by the app after it has received a state notification to suspend - and it has actually suspended. However it can also be called out of the blue, if for example in the Netflix case where you can exist the app via a menu, which will cause it to suspend rather than shutdown.

request.name: set_hibernate_ready

description.summary: signals the window manager that the app is ready to be hibernated

request.description: If an app supports hibernation it should call this when in the suspended state, and it is safe to now hibernate. The system may then at some point later move the apps state to hibernated and freeze / hibernate the app.
